newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW - SENTRA BETS ON EFFICIENCY - CEO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - SENTRA BETS ON EFFICIENCY - CEO.

text.p: After an acquisition quintupling its net sales, Finnish retail group Sentra Oy plans to compete through efficiency, its chief executive said on Tuesday.
"We intend to be the Finland's most efficient daily goods retailer," Bjorn Westerholm told Reuters in an interview.

This will come partly from the group's 35 percent stake in wholesale supplier TukoSpar and partly from the potential benefits of focusing marketing resources on a single chain name and one brand name, Spar, Westerholm said.
"We stand to save -- not by spending less (on marketing) but by getting more, and more efficient, advertising with the same money," Westerholm said.

A week and a half ago, Sentra bought Suomen Spar Oy, a chain of 350 Spar markets and shops, and a 35 percent stake in wholesaler TukoSpar Oy, paying a total of 335 million markka to Kesko-controlled Tuko.

The deal -- part of a series as retailer Kesko unbundled some elements in its purchase of former rival Tuko to meet EU competition concerns -- makes Sentra the biggest company on the Helsinki bourse's OTC list in terms of sales.
It still needs approval from the European Union's competition officials, who blocked Kesko's acquisition of Tuko last autumn saying it would hinder competition.

But the market at least does not expect any problems: Sentra's stock has more than doubled, from about 150 markka before the deal, to a life high of 360.00 afterwards. On Tuesday, it traded around 355.00 markka.
Mainly domestic investors have driven the stock and at current levels analysts say they are starting to find Sentra pricey -- but it has clearly undergone a deep revaluation.

Adding the new shops -- 300 of which are owned by independent merchants forming a captive clientele for TukoSpar wholesales -- to the 30 outlets it already owned, Sentra will form a chain with annual sales of about four billion markka.

"The main focus will be on steering the Spar chain. That means Sentra will focus entirely on the Spar chain name and reinforce the identity of the different parts of the chain under the Spar umbrella," Westerholm said.
Once it shifts to just one chain name and one brand, Sentra will be able to concentrate all its resources on making that brand known, Westerholm said.

Before the deal, Sentra had three daily goods chains, Prima, Rabatti and EuroSpar. It also had Carrols, a fast-food chain, which it sold to Tuko for 90 million markka at the same time as it bought Suomen Spar and its TukoSpar stake.
Sentra's strategy to be a low-cost operator revolves around its participation in wholesale group TukoSpar, said Westerholm.
"We can be the most efficient retailer because we will have Finland's most efficient logistics company, TukoSpar, behind us," Westerholm said.
"TukoSpar is almost a non-profit operation. Of course it covers its own costs ... But its main task is not to make a profit," he said.
Westerholm sees no difficulty in digesting its new acquisitions and managing growth.

"We bought all of Suomen Spar, in other words a ready-made company with a functioning organisation and a good management," Westerholm said. "The changes that will be made will be as small as possible."

Despite growing five-fold in terms of sales, Sentra's payroll will only rise to about 1,200 from the current 1,100 as the divested Carrols chain had almost as many employees as the new operations, Westerholm said.
